decisionsMade.decision: NeutralToneMapping in three.js, AgX in Blender
decisionsMade.why: ACESFilmic desaturates hot saturated values toward white. Doc 17 explicitly screens for gold flattening to yellow and red drifting orange, which is that exact artifact.

decisionsMade.decision: clone + selective material.clone() for multiplayer, not onBeforeCompile or InstancedMesh
decisionsMade.why: Verified against three 0.186.1 source: Material.clone() copies scalars and colors but keeps texture pointers, so no map is re-uploaded, and MeshStandardMaterial is a fixed uber-shader so no recompile. InstancedMesh would cost per-bike frustum culling for a draw-call win that is irrelevant at 2-6 bikes.

decisionsMade.decision: one shared UnrealBloomPass with threshold above the body materials' peak
decisionsMade.why: Bloom is applied post-color, so each player's hue survives a single pass. Per-player passes are only needed if art direction wants different bloom radii, not different hues.

decisionsMade.decision: 11 materials exactly as the doc names them
decisionsMade.why: The doc also calls for dark anodized aluminum and blackened steel as distinct looks but names only two metal slots. Rather than invent a 12th material, MAT_LC_BRUSHED_METAL carries both at a dark base color. Flagged rather than silently resolved.
Verified empirically: ACTIONS yields glTF animations named verbatim after the Blender Actions. ACTIVE_ACTIONS yields zero once the active action is cleared, and SCENE names them after objects.

decisionsMade.decision: Viro energy is Constant + Add diffuse, not emission
decisionsMade.why: ViroMaterial has no emissiveColor, emissiveIntensity or emissiveTexture. The native engine has the pipeline but only the glTF importer populates it, and a surface shader modifier cannot reach it. Unlit additive is the documented Viro substitute.

decisionsMade.decision: every Viro player mints uniquely-suffixed material names
decisionsMade.why: ViroMaterials is one global name-keyed registry. Two players sharing MAT_LC_EMISSIVE_PRIMARY would mutate the same native material and share a colour.

decisionsMade.decision: material name is the only runtime handle on Viro
decisionsMade.why: Viro3DObject exposes no node lookup, and materials/shaderOverrides are whole-model. LC_Reactor_Ring_A cannot be targeted at runtime. The spec already gives every independently-controlled region its own material slot, so the architecture survives unchanged.

decisionsMade.decision: the bike moves to fit the rider, not the reverse
decisionsMade.why: Doc section 15. Segment lengths are fixed human anatomy; control positions are a design choice, so the solver reports where the rider lands and the deck table follows.

decisionsMade.decision: gltfpack is a separate post-process, never a flag on the Blender export
decisionsMade.why: Default gltfpack destroys 5 contractual nodes (LC_Reactor_Core, LC_FX_TrailOrigin, LC_FX_Boost, LC_FX_CrashCenter, LC_FX_DerezCenter) and fails the validator; -kn fixes it but Blender's export_gltfpack_kn defaults to False. Blender also writes to a gltfpacked/ subdirectory and swallows CalledProcessError, so a failed pack reports success. Calling gltfpack directly makes a failure a failure, and keeps the canonical GLB as the thing CI validates.

decisionsMade.decision: losing node extras to gltfpack is acceptable
decisionsMade.why: gltfpack strips all extras with no flag to keep them, but the lc_* tags are DCC-side bookkeeping. The runtime reads spec/ for node roles and never the GLB's extras, so nothing downstream depends on them.

openQuestions: UNVERIFIED on device: whether one Viro3DObject can run several named clips at once on different sub-nodes. ViroAnimation is a singular config, which would break independent wheel and reactor motion in XR.

UNVERIFIED on device: whether shaderOverrides on separate Viro3DObject instances truly isolates per-player material state, or whether the global registry leaks across instances. The entire XR multiplayer colour story rests on this.
